name: Liberia
tagline: Sapo, surf, and the last of the Upper Guinean forest
summary: Sapo National Park holds pygmy hippo and forest elephant in the second largest block of rainforest in West Africa, Robertsport has the best surf on the coast, and Monrovia was founded by freed American slaves in 1822.
when: November to April. The rains are extraordinary — Monrovia gets over four metres a year.

entries.caption: Sapo
entries.description: Rainforest with pygmy hippo, forest elephant and chimpanzee, and no road into most of it.
entries.subject: closed rainforest canopy and a river in Sapo National Park

entries.caption: The Upper Guinean Forest
entries.description: Liberia holds about forty per cent of what is left of it.
entries.subject: buttressed rainforest trees and lianas in Liberian forest

entries.caption: The Pygmy Hippo
entries.description: Nocturnal, solitary, forest-dwelling, and one of the rarest large mammals in Africa.
entries.subject: a pygmy hippo at the edge of a forest stream at night

entries.caption: Forest Tracking
entries.description: There is no game drive here. Sapo is walked, with trackers, over days.
entries.subject: a tracker on a forest path in Sapo National Park

entries.caption: Mount Nimba and Wologizi
entries.description: Nimba on the Guinean border, and the Wologizi range with the highest ground in the country.
entries.subject: the forested Wologizi range under cloud

entries.caption: Kpatawee
entries.description: Falls over granite ledges into a swimmable pool in Bong county.
entries.subject: the Kpatawee waterfall falling over granite into a pool

entries.caption: The Saint Paul and the Cavalla
entries.description: The Saint Paul runs past Monrovia; the Cavalla marks the whole Ivorian border.
entries.subject: the Saint Paul river running wide through forest

entries.caption: Five Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Long empty beaches, and a serious swell from November on.
entries.subject: an empty palm-backed beach on the Liberian Atlantic coast

entries.caption: Sapo and Gola
entries.description: Two blocks of high forest, both transboundary, and the best-protected in the region.
entries.subject: mist rising off rainforest canopy at dawn in Sapo

entries.caption: Surfing Robertsport
entries.description: Cassava Point and Fisherman's Point — long left-hand point breaks, and a village surf club.
entries.subject: a surfer on a long left-hand wave at Robertsport

entries.caption: Americo-Liberian and Sixteen Others
entries.description: A settler republic founded in 1822 over sixteen indigenous peoples, and the tension of that.
entries.subject: a nineteenth-century settler house with a verandah in Monrovia

entries.caption: Kpelle, Bassa, Grebo, Vai
entries.description: The Vai invented their own script in the 1830s, one of very few in Africa.
entries.subject: carved Vai script characters on a wooden board

entries.caption: Jollof, Palm Butter and Fufu
entries.description: Palm butter soup, cassava fufu, and a jollof Liberians will argue about at length.
entries.subject: a bowl of palm butter soup with rice and fish

entries.caption: Independence Day
entries.description: 26 July, and the parades, the food and the noise that come with it.
entries.subject: an Independence Day parade in the streets of Monrovia

entries.caption: Masks and Country Cloth
entries.description: Poro and Sande society masks in the interior, and woven country cloth everywhere.
entries.subject: a carved wooden Dan mask with a smooth blackened surface

entries.caption: Providence Island
entries.description: Where the first settlers landed in 1822, in the middle of Monrovia's harbour.
entries.subject: the old cotton tree and monument on Providence Island

entries.caption: A Republic Built by the Freed
entries.description: Monrovia's nineteenth-century houses are the architecture of a return that did not go simply.
entries.subject: a decaying nineteenth-century settler mansion in Monrovia

entries.caption: Monrovia
entries.description: A capital on a peninsula between the Atlantic and the Mesurado, rebuilt and rebuilding.
entries.subject: the waterfront and low skyline of Monrovia

entries.caption: Verandah and Zinc
entries.description: Americo-Liberian timber houses with deep verandahs, and zinc-roofed cityscape behind them.
entries.subject: a timber verandah house with a zinc roof in Monrovia

entries.caption: The Beach at Sinkor
entries.description: Monrovia goes to the beach bars along Sinkor at the weekend, and stays.
entries.subject: beach bars and crowds along the shore at Sinkor, Monrovia

entries.caption: Kpatawee and the Coast
entries.description: A waterfall pool inland and calm bays on the coast, both easy days out.
entries.subject: children swimming in the pool below Kpatawee falls

entries.caption: Sapo on Foot
entries.description: Multi-day forest walking with rangers, sleeping in camps, and no vehicles at all.
entries.subject: a ranger camp under tarpaulins in Sapo rainforest

entries.caption: Beginning
entries.description: Beach lodges at Robertsport and a few good hotels in Monrovia.
entries.subject: a simple beach lodge under palms at Robertsport

entries.caption: Forty Per Cent of What Is Left
entries.description: Liberia's forest is the largest surviving piece of the Upper Guinean block.
entries.subject: an aerial view of unbroken rainforest canopy in Liberia

entries.caption: Green and Water
entries.description: Sapo after rain, when the canopy drips and the light comes through in shafts.
entries.subject: shafts of light through wet rainforest canopy in Sapo

entries.caption: Lake Piso
entries.description: A lagoon behind Robertsport with mangrove, fishing villages and no visitors.
entries.subject: fishing canoes on the still water of Lake Piso

entries.caption: Why Liberia
entries.description: The best surf in West Africa, and the forest the pygmy hippo has left.
entries.subject: a lone surfer walking a long empty beach at Robertsport
